load_bearing_primary.interpretation: A capability is chosen by what the sentence's verb acts ON, not by which verbs the sentence contains, and a sentence that names a route has chosen it. 'write the repair REPORT' and 'write the FIX' are the same verb in different frames, and only the second is a request to overwrite the input; VerbNet's frames and FrameNet's frame elements are the established statement of that distinction, and the machine already had both capabilities, so nothing had to be built -- only the sentence had to be read the same way by all five readers.
load_bearing_primary.measured_effect: FIXED-SEED A/B, 37 families x 6 fresh instances plus 20 out-of-scope, seed 424242, before = main 7913c4d and after = this branch. BEFORE in-scope 0.6852 (152/222), out-of-scope 20/20. AFTER in-scope 0.8241 (183/222), out-of-scope 20/20, ZERO families down. Five families moved 0/6 -> 6/6: PYTHON_AST_PATCH_SEARCH, PYTHON_REPAIR_COUPLED_AST, PYTHON_REPAIR_COUPLED_PROV, PYTHON_REPAIR_STRICT_PROGRESS and YAML_TO_JSON. The five repair families were then re-measured at five seeds (7, 11, 99, 1234, 424242) x 6 instances: 150/150 PASS, where 11 is the seed at which the coupled pair failed before the instrument fix. SEVEN CAUSES MEASURED, EACH BY RUNNING THE REAL SENTENCE, NOT INFERRED. (1) Route admission tested for a command slot literally named `argv`, and the six repair entries declare `test_argv`; composer_route_v1.bind filled that slot correctly with ['python3','.../test_x.py'], so three families were refused NO_COMMAND_SLOT_FOR_THE_STATED_COMMAND although the sentence, the ranking and the binding were all right. (2) python.patch.search.test_guided.ast.v1 writes source_path and unified_diff at the TOP LEVEL of its report while the coupled loops nest the same two fields under patches, and the promise reader only read report['patches']. (3) The door's repair-verb regex matched the noun in 'with the test guided REPAIR loop' and in 'the REPAIR report', so every test file listed after that phrase became a repair target and the coupled goals were refused PROMISED_SOURCE_UNCHANGED:<test file> -- a promise no repair can ever keep, because a repair does not edit its own witnesses. (4) A stated source ROOT was handled as if it were a file, so 'Repair the python source root DIR' demanded a change to the witness test inside DIR. (5) `write` occurs in the provides of python.software.repair.apply.verified.v1, so 'With the test guided repair loop, repair ... AND WRITE THE REPAIR REPORT to R' ranked the in-place writer first and it overwrote the source, which the family oracle forbids; the same request phrased with `save` reached the loop. Routing was decided by which synonym the caller used. (6) The coupled generator's goal named only the coupled test while its oracle ran all three test files on disk, so a patch satisfying the one stated equation was rejected by a condition the sentence never stated. (7) The patch-search report carried no machine-readable candidate list while its own family oracle requires one: `patches` was simply absent from the schema it wrote.
